title: Patterns in the Sky
seo_title: Grade 1 Science: Patterns in the Sky Worksheets (BC Curriculum)
standard_text: Observable patterns and cycles occur in the local sky and landscape: common objects in the sky (Sun, Moon, stars), day and night, local weather patterns and the four seasons, and First Peoples knowledge of the sky. (summary of BC's Curriculum, Science 1, Earth and Space Science)
meta_desc: Free Grade 1 science worksheets (BC): day and night, the Sun in the sky, the Moon and stars, daylight and the seasons. 100 picture questions with answers.
key_big: Sky patterns repeat each day and year.
key_sub: The Sun rises in the east and sets in the west.
body_html:
How to think about it

The sky has patterns that repeat.

  • The Sun rises, crosses the sky and sets.
  • We see the Moon and stars at night.
  • Summer days are long; winter days are short.
Example

When can we see the stars?

The Sun is too bright in the day.

Answer: at night

Example

Which season has the longest days?

The Sun is up the longest.

Answer: summer

Common mistakes

  • Thinking the Sun moves around Earth.
  • Thinking the Moon is only out at night.
